Final examination 9 October 2014. Reitzenstein confirmed as referee/supervisor in OPUS Würzburg repository record.

short_bio: Tobias Heindel is Professor of Photonic Quantum Networks at the Department for Quantum Technology, University of Münster. He is one of Germany's leading experimentalists in semiconductor quantum photonics, specialising in the development of high-purity quantum dot single-photon sources and their deployment in quantum key distribution (QKD) and photonic quantum networks.

name: Hugo Zbinden
short_bio: Hugo Zbinden (born 1961, Bern) is Honorary Professor of Physics at the University of Geneva, where he spent more than three decades at the Department of Applied Physics. He studied physics at the University of Bern, receiving an MSc in climate physics (1987) and a PhD in laser physics (1991). After a short postdoctoral industry project in Bern, he joined the University of Geneva in 1993 as a postdoc in Nicolas Gisin's group, was appointed MER (Maître d'enseignement et de recherche) in 1998, promoted to Associate Professor in 2012 when he launched the dedicated Quantum Technologies group, and retired in 2023 while retaining an honorary professorship. He is currently also involved in establishing the Vigo Quantum Communication Center at the University of Vigo.

name: Rupert Ursin

current_position.title: Senior Research Group Leader and Deputy Director, IQOQI Vienna (Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information)

education.note: Dissertation on quantum teleportation over long distances, completed December 2006.

short_bio: Rupert Ursin (born 26 January 1973) is an Austrian experimental physicist and Senior Research Group Leader and Deputy Director at IQOQI Vienna (Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information, Austrian Academy of Sciences). He completed his PhD in 2006 at the University of Vienna under Anton Zeilinger, working on quantum teleportation over long distances. He is best known for distributing entangled photons over a 144 km free-space link between the Canary Islands (La Palma–Tenerife, 2007), and for co-authoring the first experimental demonstration of free-space decoy-state QKD over 144 km (PRL, 2007). He contributed to the Micius satellite-relayed intercontinental quantum network demonstration (PRL, 2018) and to the significant-loophole-free Bell test with entangled photons (PRL, 2015). He has received the Christian-Doppler-Prize (2009) and the Gründungspreis Phönix (2023), and is also CEO of Quantum Technology Laboratories GmbH.

name: Marco Bellini

education.note: PhD in Physics from University of Firenze (1992 MSc, 1996 PhD). Advisor name not found in accessible sources; early career work was in ultrafast/harmonic spectroscopy at LENS Florence.

short_bio: Marco Bellini is a physicist at the National Institute of Optics (CNR-INO) in Florence working on experimental quantum optics. His group engineers non-classical states of light through single-photon addition and subtraction, probing the particle-wave nature of light and continuous-variable quantum states.

name: Jeremy L. O'Brien

education.note: PhD in Physics from UNSW 2002; experimental work on correlated and confined electrons in organic conductors, superconductors and semiconductor nanostructures, and progress towards phosphorus-in-silicon quantum computer; advisor not found in accessible sources

short_bio: Jeremy L. O'Brien is an experimental quantum physicist who pioneered integrated quantum photonics and co-founded PsiQuantum, the world's largest quantum computing start-up by funding. He received his PhD in physics from the University of New South Wales in 2002, then held a research fellowship at the University of Queensland (2001–2006) before becoming Professor of Physics and Electrical Engineering at the University of Bristol (2006–2016), where he founded and directed the Centre for Quantum Photonics (CQP) and the Quantum Engineering Technology Labs (QET Labs). In 2016 he co-founded PsiQuantum with Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson to build utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers using a silicon photonics manufacturing platform. He served as CEO until February 2026, when he became Executive Chairman. O'Brien demonstrated the first optical two-qubit CNOT gate (Nature, 2003), invented integrated quantum photonics by implementing quantum circuits on silica-on-silicon waveguide chips (Science, 2008), and co-invented the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) algorithm on a photonic processor (Nature Communications, 2014). His group built the first universal linear optics processor (Science, 2015) and implemented Shor's factoring algorithm on a photonic chip (Science, 2009). He holds an h-index of 92 with over 51,000 citations.

name: Terry Rudolph
short_bio: Terry Rudolph is a theoretical physicist at Imperial College London and a co-founder of PsiQuantum. His work develops photonic quantum computing, including measurement-based and fusion-based architectures that build large entangled cluster states from single photons for fault-tolerant computation.

name: Sven Ramelow

current_position.title: Assistant Professor and Emmy Noether Group Leader (Nonlinear Quantum Optics)

short_bio: Sven Ramelow is a physicist at Humboldt University of Berlin working on quantum optics and quantum imaging. His group develops entangled-photon sources, nonlinear interferometry and imaging with undetected photons using quantum correlations.

name: Gerd Leuchs

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light
current_position.title: Director Emeritus

short_bio: Gerd Leuchs (born 14 June 1950) is a German experimental physicist and Director Emeritus at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light (MPL) in Erlangen, Germany, and Senior Professor (emeritus) at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU). He is one of the pioneering figures in continuous-variable (CV) quantum information and quantum optics, with foundational contributions to squeezed light, fiber-optical quantum communication, quantum key distribution, and polarization-structured light.

name: Akira Furusawa
short_bio: Akira Furusawa (born 1961) is a Japanese experimental physicist and Professor in the Department of Applied Physics, School of Engineering, at the University of Tokyo. He is one of the world's foremost authorities on continuous-variable (CV) quantum information science, best known for leading the first experimental demonstration of unconditional quantum teleportation (Science 1998) and for pioneering the generation of ultra-large-scale CV cluster states as a resource for measurement-based optical quantum computing.

name: Stephanie Wehner

current_position.title: Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Professor in Quantum Information

thesis.title: Cryptography in a Quantum World
thesis.note: PhD thesis at CWI Amsterdam; advisor Harry Buhrman

short_bio: Stephanie Wehner is the Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Professor in Quantum Information at Delft University of Technology / QuTech, and Director of the European Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA). Her research spans quantum cryptography, quantum communication protocols, and the architectural foundations of a large-scale quantum internet.

name: Hugues de Riedmatten

current_position.institution: ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences
current_position.title: ICREA Professor and Group Leader, Quantum Photonics with Solids and Atoms

education.note: Thesis no. 3480: Photonic entanglement in optical fibers: from long distance quantum teleportation to high-dimensional Hilbert spaces; Group of Applied Physics, University of Geneva.

postdocs.note: Postdoc in the Kimble quantum optics group at Caltech. Co-authored the landmark 2005 Nature paper on measurement-induced entanglement in remote atomic ensembles (Chou, de Riedmatten, Felinto, Polyakov, van Enk, Kimble, Nature 438, 2005).

Returned to Geneva as senior scientist in the Gisin group after Caltech postdoc; led solid-state quantum memory experiments including the foundational AFC memory and first solid-state photonic entanglement storage results.

short_bio: Hugues de Riedmatten is ICREA Professor and head of the Quantum Photonics with Solids and Atoms (QPSA) group at ICFO — The Institute of Photonic Sciences in Castelldefels, Spain, a position he has held since 2010. He is one of the world's leading experimentalists in quantum memories for light and quantum repeater hardware, with particular expertise in rare-earth-ion-doped crystals and cold atomic ensembles.

name: Mikael Afzelius

current_position.title: Maître d'enseignement et de recherche (Senior Lecturer)

education.note: Afzelius's earliest Geneva publications date to ~2008; PhD advisor inferred as Gisin based on group membership and co-authorship; no primary thesis record found in public databases

short_bio: Mikael Afzelius is a Maître d'enseignement et de recherche (senior lecturer/MER) in the Department of Applied Physics at the University of Geneva, where he leads the qram (Quantum Repeaters and Memories) group. He is best known as a co-inventor of the atomic frequency comb (AFC) quantum memory protocol, introduced in a landmark 2009 Physical Review A paper with Christoph Simon, Hugues de Riedmatten, and Nicolas Gisin, which proposed storing light in an inhomogeneously broadened optical transition spectrally shaped into a periodic comb structure and has since become one of the most widely used protocols for rare-earth quantum memories.

current_position.institution: Institut de Physique Théorique (IPhT), CEA/CNRS/Université Paris-Saclay
current_position.title: Directeur de recherche CEA

name: Wolfgang Tittel

current_position.title: Professor and Chair (UNIGE / Constructor University joint chair)

short_bio: Wolfgang Tittel (born c. 1969, Germany) is Professor and Chair in Quantum Communications at the University of Geneva, holding a joint appointment with Constructor University established in January 2023. He is one of the leading experimental physicists in quantum communication over optical fibre, with foundational contributions to long-distance quantum entanglement distribution, quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation, and solid-state quantum memories for quantum repeaters.

name: William D. Oliver

current_position.title: Henry Ellis Warren (1894) Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Professor of Physics

postdocs.note: Mentored Jonas Bylander (165-jonas-bylander) as postdoc at MIT RLE / Lincoln Laboratory 2008–2012; noise spectroscopy and dynamical decoupling collaboration

short_bio: William Oliver is an experimental physicist at MIT, where he directs superconducting quantum-computing research across campus and MIT Lincoln Laboratory. His group works on transmon and fluxonium qubits, qubit materials and coherence, high-fidelity gates and readout, and scalable superconducting processor architectures; he is a co-author of widely used reviews ('A quantum engineer's guide to superconducting qubits').

name: Travis Humble

current_position.title: Director, Quantum Science Center; Distinguished Scientist

short_bio: Travis Humble is a Distinguished Scientist at Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Director of the Quantum Science Center, working on quantum computing architectures, the integration of quantum processors with high-performance computing, and the benchmarking and verification of quantum hardware across platforms.

name: Ivan Deutsch

current_position.title: Regents' Professor of Physics & Astronomy; Director, Center for Quantum Information and Control (CQuIC)

short_bio: Ivan Deutsch is Regents' Professor of Physics at the University of New Mexico and a theorist of quantum information science. His work develops quantum control, measurement and tomography for atomic systems, including neutral-atom and trapped-ion qubits and Rydberg-mediated interactions, and the theory of continuous measurement and feedback.

name: Nir Davidson

education.note: Doctoral work in diffractive and laser optics in the group of Asher A. Friesem (inferred from early publication record).

postdocs.note: Postdoctoral research on atom optics and dark (blue-detuned) optical dipole traps for cold atoms in the group of Nobel laureate Steven Chu.

keywords: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates
short_bio: Prof. Nir Davidson is an experimental physicist in the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads a cold-atom and laser-physics laboratory. His research spans the dynamics and precision spectroscopy of ultracold atoms, quantum-degenerate Bose and Fermi gases, atom interferometry, coupled-laser networks, and slow and stored light in hot atomic vapor.

name: Ofer Firstenberg

education.note: Completed within the IDF Talpiot program.
Doctoral research carried out at Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, co-supervised by Amiram Ron (Technion) and Nir Davidson (Weizmann).

postdocs.institution: Harvard University / MIT (Harvard-MIT Center for Ultracold Atoms)
postdocs.note: Postdoctoral research at the Harvard-MIT Center for Ultracold Atoms; led the experiments demonstrating photonic molecules (bound states of photons) in a Rydberg medium.

keywords: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates
short_bio: Prof. Ofer Firstenberg is an experimental physicist in the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads the **Light-vs-Matter Lab**. His research asks whether individual photons can be made to behave like massive particles — and atoms like light — through strong, controllable photon-photon interactions. The group works on photon-photon interaction in cold Rydberg gases (photonic molecules and crystals), hot quantum memories spanning nanoseconds to hours, and atom interferometry.

name: Tom Manovitz

education.note: Doctoral research on trapped-ion quantum computing with robust entangling gates and quantum coherent feedback.

postdocs.institution: Harvard University (Max Planck-Harvard Center for Quantum Optics)
postdocs.note: Four years in the Lukin group developing reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays; contributed to back-to-back Nature papers on logical qubits and high-fidelity entangling gates.

keywords: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

thesis.title: Trapped-ion quantum computing with robust entangling gates and quantum coherent feedback

short_bio: Dr. Tom Manovitz is an experimental physicist who joined the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science in October 2025, where he leads a new laboratory using high-resolution laser arrays to trap and manipulate individual neutral atoms as a platform for building and probing large, highly entangled quantum systems. His group focuses on entanglement and quantum many-body physics, hardware for neutral-atom quantum processors, and quantum computation and error correction.

name: Serge Rosenblum

education.note: Doctoral research on single-atom quantum optics — all-optical single-photon routing and single-photon extraction with an atom-cavity system.

postdocs.note: Postdoctoral research in circuit QED — error-correctable bosonic qubits encoded in superconducting microwave cavities, including a CNOT gate between cavity qubits.

thesis.title: Single-photon quantum optics with a single atom

short_bio: Dr. Serge Rosenblum is an experimental physicist at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where his group builds superconducting quantum circuits for quantum information processing. His research centers on circuit QED and error-correctable **bosonic qubits** encoded in long-lived superconducting microwave cavities, aiming at hardware-efficient quantum error correction.

name: Daniel Zajfman

current_position.title: Professor of Physics (Particle Physics and Astrophysics)

postdocs.note: Postdoctoral research in atomic and molecular physics (1989–1991).

keywords: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

thesis.title: Unknown

short_bio: Prof. Daniel Zajfman is an experimental physicist in the Department of Particle Physics and Astrophysics at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where his group ("Molecular Physics and Ion Trapping," with Dr. Oded Heber) studies the dynamics of single atomic, molecular, and cluster ions. He is a pioneer of the **electrostatic ion beam trap** — a linear "electrostatic bottle" that stores fast ion beams between facing electrostatic mirrors without magnetic fields — and uses such traps and storage rings to recreate the extreme conditions of interstellar space in the laboratory, probing dissociative recombination, internal decay processes, and the surprising self-bunching of trapped ions.

name: Barak Dayan

education.note: Doctoral research on nonlinear and quantum optics with broadband down-converted (entangled) light.

postdocs.note: Postdoctoral research in cavity QED in the Kimble group; demonstrated a single-atom photon turnstile using an atom coupled to a microtoroidal resonator.

keywords: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

thesis.title: Nonlinear optics with broadband down-converted light

short_bio: Prof. Barak Dayan is an experimental physicist in the Department of Chemical and Biological Physics at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads the **Quantum Optics group**. His research centers on achieving deterministic photon-photon interactions at the single-photon level — using laser-cooled atoms coupled to optical microresonators to let a single atom, or even a single photon, control another photon. His group demonstrated a single-atom all-optical switch and a passive photon-atom quantum gate, foundational primitives for photonic quantum information.

name: John Preskill

current_position.title: Richard P. Feynman Professor of Theoretical Physics; Director, Institute for Quantum Information and Matter (IQIM)

short_bio: John Preskill is a theoretical physicist at Caltech and director of the Institute for Quantum Information and Matter. He coined the term "quantum supremacy" and the NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) era, and is a leading voice on quantum error correction, fault tolerance, and the theory of quantum information.

name: Ignacio Cirac

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics
current_position.title: Director, Theory Division

short_bio: J. Ignacio Cirac is a theoretical physicist and director of the Theory Division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics. With Peter Zoller he proposed the 1995 Cirac-Zoller scheme for a trapped-ion quantum gate -- the blueprint for much of trapped-ion quantum computing -- and has made foundational contributions to quantum simulation and tensor-network methods.

name: Serge Haroche
short_bio: Serge Haroche is a French physicist who shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics with David Wineland for ground-breaking experimental methods that enable measuring and manipulating individual quantum systems. At the Ecole Normale Superieure and College de France he pioneered cavity quantum electrodynamics, trapping single photons and probing them non-destructively with Rydberg atoms.

name: Alain Aspect
short_bio: Alain Aspect shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments with entangled photons that established the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneered quantum information science. A professor at the Institut d'Optique, he is also a co-founder of the neutral-atom quantum-computing company Pasqal.

name: Carl Wieman

current_position.title: Professor of Physics and of Education (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

short_bio: Carl Wieman shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics with Eric Cornell and Wolfgang Ketterle for creating the first Bose-Einstein condensate in a dilute gas of rubidium atoms (1995) at JILA. He is now a professor at Stanford, also renowned for his work on science education.

name: Eric A. Cornell

current_position.institution: University of Colorado Boulder / JILA / NIST
current_position.title: Professor of Physics; NIST Fellow (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

short_bio: Eric Cornell shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics for producing, with Carl Wieman, the first gaseous Bose-Einstein condensate at JILA in 1995. A NIST and University of Colorado physicist, he continues to lead precision-measurement and ultracold-atom research.

name: Wolfgang Ketterle

current_position.title: John D. MacArthur Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

short_bio: Wolfgang Ketterle shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics for achieving Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute atomic gases and for early fundamental studies of the condensates' properties. At MIT he leads research on ultracold atoms and quantum simulation of many-body physics.

name: William D. Phillips

current_position.title: NIST Fellow & Distinguished University Professor (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1997)

short_bio: William D. Phillips shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics with Steven Chu and Claude Cohen-Tannoudji for developing methods to cool and trap atoms with laser light. A NIST Fellow and co-founder of the Joint Quantum Institute, he works on ultracold atoms, atom optics, and quantum simulation.

name: Steven Chu

current_position.title: William R. Kenan Jr. Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1997)

short_bio: Steven Chu shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for the laser cooling and trapping of atoms. A professor at Stanford, he later served as the 12th U.S. Secretary of Energy (2009-2013) and mentored a generation of atomic physicists, including Nir Davidson.

name: Theodor W. Hansch

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics / LMU Munich
current_position.title: Director; Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2005)

short_bio: Theodor W. Hansch shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics for contributions to laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency-comb technique. He directs a division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and is a professor at LMU Munich.

name: Jean Dalibard

current_position.institution: College de France / Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, ENS
current_position.title: Professor

short_bio: Jean Dalibard is a French physicist at the College de France and Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, known for foundational work on laser cooling (Sisyphus cooling, the magneto-optical trap), quantum gases, and synthetic gauge fields in ultracold atoms.

name: Gerhard Rempe

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics
current_position.title: Director, Quantum Dynamics Division

short_bio: Gerhard Rempe directs the Quantum Dynamics Division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics. His group pioneered cavity quantum electrodynamics with single atoms, deterministic atom-photon entanglement, and elementary quantum networks and quantum logic with light.

name: H. Jeff Kimble

current_position.title: William L. Valentine Professor and Professor of Physics, Emeritus

short_bio: H. Jeff Kimble is a pioneer of experimental quantum optics and cavity QED at Caltech. His group demonstrated landmark results in photon antibunching, quantum teleportation of light, and the concept of the "quantum internet" built from atom-photon interfaces.

name: Anton Zeilinger
short_bio: Anton Zeilinger shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments with entangled photons establishing Bell-inequality violations and pioneering quantum information science. Based at the University of Vienna, he demonstrated quantum teleportation and long-distance entanglement distribution.

name: Jean-Michel Raimond
short_bio: Jean-Michel Raimond is a French physicist at Sorbonne Universite and the Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, where, with Serge Haroche, he developed cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments probing the quantum-to-classical transition with Rydberg atoms and microwave photons.

name: Philippe Grangier

current_position.institution: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique / CNRS
current_position.title: Research Director (CNRS)

short_bio: Philippe Grangier is a CNRS physicist at the Institut d'Optique whose early experiments demonstrated single-photon behaviour and wave-particle duality. His group pioneered single-atom trapping in optical tweezers and Rydberg-atom quantum gates, foundational to neutral-atom quantum computing.

name: John L. Hall

current_position.institution: JILA / NIST / University of Colorado Boulder
current_position.title: Senior Scientist Emeritus (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2005)

short_bio: John L. 'Jan' Hall shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics for contributions to laser-based precision spectroscopy and the optical frequency-comb technique. A long-time JILA/NIST scientist, his work underpins modern optical atomic clocks and precision measurement.

name: Marlan O. Scully
short_bio: Marlan O. Scully is a theoretical physicist at Texas A&M (and affiliated with Princeton and Baylor) known for foundational work in quantum optics, including the laser phase-transition analogy, lasing without inversion, the micromaser, and quantum coherence effects. He co-authored the standard text Quantum Optics.

name: Hans Dehmelt

current_position.title: Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1989)

postdocs.note: Microwave spectroscopy; began developing ion- and electron-trapping techniques.

short_bio: Hans Georg Dehmelt (1922–2017) was a German-American physicist who shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing the ion-trap (Penning-trap) technique. After a doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Hans Kopfermann and postdoctoral work at Duke University with Walter Gordy, he joined the University of Washington, where his group isolated and observed a single trapped barium ion and a single electron confined as "geonium," enabling the most precise measurement of the electron magnetic moment (g-factor) and founding the field of single-particle precision spectroscopy that underlies modern trapped-ion quantum computing.

name: Norman F. Ramsey

current_position.title: Higgins Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1989)

short_bio: Norman F. Ramsey shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physics for the separated oscillatory fields method (Ramsey interferometry) and the invention of the hydrogen maser. His techniques are the basis of atomic clocks and precision spectroscopy. A Harvard professor, he died in 2011.

name: Dorit Aharonov
short_bio: Dorit Aharonov is a theoretical computer scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem renowned for the quantum threshold theorem (fault-tolerant quantum computation), adiabatic quantum computing, and quantum complexity. She is a co-founder and chief scientific officer of the quantum-error-mitigation company Qedma.

name: Netanel Lindner
short_bio: Netanel Lindner is a theoretical condensed-matter and quantum-information physicist at the Technion, known for work on topological phases, Floquet engineering, and quantum error characterization. He is a co-founder and CTO of the quantum-error-mitigation company Qedma.

name: Shay Hacohen-Gourgy
short_bio: Shay Hacohen-Gourgy is an experimental physicist at the Technion specializing in superconducting quantum circuits, quantum measurement, and feedback control. He is a co-founder and CTO of QuamCore, a startup developing a scalable superconducting quantum processor.

name: Yoav Sagi
short_bio: Yoav Sagi is an experimental physicist at the Technion leading an ultracold-atoms laboratory focused on quantum-degenerate Fermi gases and many-body physics. He is a co-founder of the neutral-atom quantum-computing startup Q-Factor.

name: A. Paul Alivisatos

current_position.title: President of the University of Chicago; Professor of Chemistry

short_bio: A. Paul Alivisatos is a chemist and president of the University of Chicago, internationally known for pioneering work on semiconductor nanocrystals (quantum dots) and their applications.

name: Aharon Kapitulnik

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

short_bio: Aharon Kapitulnik is a condensed-matter physicist at Stanford studying superconductivity, quantum materials and high-precision measurement.

name: Alex Kuzmich
short_bio: Alex Kuzmich is an experimental physicist known for pioneering work on quantum memories and entanglement in atomic ensembles for quantum networking.

name: Alex Retzker
short_bio: Alex Retzker is a theoretical physicist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem working on quantum information, quantum sensing with NV centers and trapped ions, and quantum control.

name: Alexander Gaeta

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Materials Science

short_bio: Alexander Gaeta is an experimental physicist at Columbia known for nonlinear and quantum nanophotonics, including chip-scale frequency combs and quantum light sources.

name: Alexander Pines
short_bio: Alexander Pines is a chemist at UC Berkeley renowned for foundational advances in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and magnetic resonance imaging.

name: Alexander Sergienko

current_position.title: Professor of Electrical & Computer Engineering and of Physics

short_bio: Alexander Sergienko is an experimental physicist at Boston University working on quantum optics, entangled-photon sources, and quantum communication.

name: Anatole Abragam
short_bio: Anatole Abragam was a French physicist and a founding figure of nuclear magnetic resonance, author of the classic text The Principles of Nuclear Magnetism. He died in 2011.

name: Andrew Steane
short_bio: Andrew M. Steane is a Professor of Physics at the University of Oxford and a fellow of Exeter College. He co-discovered quantum error correction — the CSS/"Steane" codes — and initiated Oxford's trapped-ion quantum-computing experiments, which he later co-led with David Lucas using calcium-ion (⁴⁰Ca⁺ and ⁴³Ca⁺) qubits. He received the Institute of Physics Maxwell Medal and Prize in 2000 and has written several physics textbooks. His work spans both the theory and experimental implementation of quantum information with trapped ions.

name: Andrew White
short_bio: Andrew White is an experimental physicist at the University of Queensland and a pioneer of photonic quantum information science and quantum process tomography.

name: Atac Imamoglu
short_bio: Atac Imamoglu is a physicist at ETH Zurich known for semiconductor quantum optics, quantum dots as single-photon sources and spin qubits, and exciton-polariton physics.

name: Beat H. Meier
short_bio: Beat H. Meier is a physical chemist at ETH Zurich recognized for advances in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: Brian Pippard
short_bio: Sir Brian Pippard was a British physicist at Cambridge, a leading figure in superconductivity and the electronic structure of metals, and a founder of Cambridge's Cavendish reforms. He died in 2008.

name: Carl Williams

current_position.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
current_position.title: Physicist; former Deputy Director, Physical Measurement Laboratory

short_bio: Carl J. Williams is a physicist at NIST who has worked on ultracold-atom theory and has been a long-standing leader of U.S. quantum-information science programs.

name: Charles Clark
short_bio: Charles W. Clark is a theoretical AMO physicist and a Fellow of the Joint Quantum Institute, with research spanning atom optics, neutron interferometry and quantum information.

name: Charles M. Marcus

current_position.institution: Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen / University of Washington
current_position.title: Professor of Physics

short_bio: Charles Marcus is an experimental physicist known for mesoscopic physics, semiconductor spin qubits and topological (Majorana) quantum-computing research.

name: Cindy A. Regal
short_bio: Cindy Regal is an experimental physicist at JILA working on optomechanics and single neutral atoms in optical tweezers for quantum information.

name: Colin Webb
short_bio: Colin Webb is a laser physicist at Oxford known for the development of gas and excimer lasers and a co-founder of Oxford Lasers.

name: Constantin Piron
short_bio: Constantin Piron was a Swiss theoretical physicist known for foundational work on quantum logic and the axiomatic structure of quantum mechanics. He died in 2019.

name: Duncan G. Steel

current_position.title: Robert J. Hiller Professor of Engineering; Professor of Physics

short_bio: Duncan G. Steel is an experimental physicist at the University of Michigan working on coherent optical control of semiconductor quantum dots and spins.

name: Dan Rugar
short_bio: Dan Rugar is a physicist at IBM Almaden who pioneered magnetic resonance force microscopy, achieving single-electron-spin detection, and nanomechanical sensing.

name: Dan Walls
short_bio: Daniel F. Walls was a New Zealand theoretical physicist and a founder of modern quantum optics theory, including squeezed states; co-author of the text Quantum Optics. He died in 1999.

name: Dana Anderson
short_bio: Dana Anderson is an experimental physicist at JILA working on atom optics and compact cold-atom systems, and a founder of ColdQuanta (now Infleqtion).

name: Daniel Prober

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

short_bio: Daniel Prober is an experimental physicist at Yale known for superconducting and nanoscale detectors, including hot-electron bolometers and single-photon sensors.

name: David DeMille
short_bio: David DeMille is an experimental atomic, molecular and optical physicist who uses polar diatomic molecules to test fundamental symmetries and search for physics beyond the Standard Model. He earned an AB in physics from the University of Chicago and a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under Eugene D. Commins, and after many years at Yale University joined Johns Hopkins University in 2024.

name: David Hall
short_bio: David Hall is an experimental physicist at Amherst College working on Bose-Einstein condensates and topological excitations such as quantum knots and monopoles.

name: David Kielpinski

postdocs.note: Co-developed the QCCD (quantum charge-coupled device) architecture for a scalable ion-trap quantum computer, using ⁹Be⁺ ions.

short_bio: David Kielpinski is a physicist known for the influential QCCD (quantum charge-coupled device) architecture for scalable trapped-ion quantum computers, developed in the NIST Ion Storage Group of David J. Wineland using ⁹Be⁺ ions (Kielpinski, Monroe & Wineland, *Nature* 2002). He later led trapped-ion and quantum-optics research at the Centre for Quantum Dynamics, Griffith University, in Brisbane, Australia.

name: Deborah Jin

current_position.institution: JILA / NIST / University of Colorado Boulder
current_position.title: Fellow, JILA/NIST (1968-2016)

short_bio: Deborah Jin was an experimental physicist at JILA who created the first fermionic condensate and pioneered ultracold polar molecules and degenerate Fermi gases. With Jun Ye, her group created the first high-phase-space-density gas of ground-state polar potassium-rubidium (KRb) molecules and demonstrated quantum-state-controlled ultracold chemistry. She died in 2016.

name: Edvardas Narevicius

current_position.title: Professor of Chemical and Biological Physics

short_bio: Edvardas Narevicius is an experimental physicist at the Weizmann Institute known for merged-beam techniques to study chemical reactions at very low temperatures (cold chemistry).

name: Evelyn Hu

current_position.title: Tarr-Coyne Professor of Applied Physics and of Electrical Engineering

short_bio: Evelyn Hu is an applied physicist at Harvard working on nanophotonics and quantum materials, including color centers and quantum-dot devices.

name: Francesco De Martini
short_bio: Francesco De Martini is an Italian experimental physicist and a pioneer of quantum optics, including quantum cloning and entangled-photon experiments.

name: Franco N. C. Wong

current_position.title: Senior Research Scientist, Research Laboratory of Electronics

short_bio: Franco Wong is a research scientist at MIT working on entangled-photon sources and quantum communication.

name: Frederic Merkt
short_bio: Frédéric Merkt is a Professor of Physical Chemistry at ETH Zurich, known for high-resolution spectroscopy of molecules and Rydberg states. His group performs precision measurements of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen and its ions (H2, H2+, HD+) as stringent tests of quantum electrodynamics, and developed Rydberg-Stark deceleration to produce slow, controlled beams of atoms and molecules.

name: Gerard Milburn
short_bio: Gerard Milburn is a theoretical physicist at the University of Queensland known for foundational work in quantum optics, quantum measurement and quantum information; co-author of Quantum Optics.

name: Gerd Schon
short_bio: Gerd Schon is a theoretical physicist at KIT known for the theory of superconducting qubits and quantum transport in nanostructures.

name: Gianni Blatter
short_bio: Gianni Blatter is a theoretical physicist at ETH Zurich known for the theory of vortices in superconductors and proposals for solid-state and superconducting qubits.

name: Gunter Werth
short_bio: Günter Werth is a German experimental physicist, Professor (emeritus) at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, known for high-precision measurements with Penning and Paul ion traps. After a doctorate at the University of Bonn (1969) he joined Mainz, led the ISOLTRAP experiment at CERN, and later headed the Cooled and Stored Ions division at the Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics in Heidelberg. His work includes precise determinations of atomic and ion g-factors and masses — using species ranging from calcium ions to highly charged ions — and tests of fundamental symmetries.

name: Guo Guangcan

current_position.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
current_position.title: Professor of Physics; CAS Academician

short_bio: Guo Guangcan is a physicist at USTC and a founder of quantum information research in China, working on quantum optics and quantum communication.

name: Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop
short_bio: Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop is an experimental physicist at the University of Queensland known for optical tweezers, laser micromanipulation and atom optics.

name: Harry Buhrman
short_bio: Harry Buhrman is a theoretical computer scientist and director of QuSoft, known for quantum complexity theory and quantum communication complexity.

name: Herbert Walther

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics / LMU Munich
current_position.title: Director (1935-2006)

short_bio: Herbert Walther was a German physicist and long-time director at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, a pioneer of cavity QED, the one-atom maser and single-ion experiments. He died in 2006.

name: Jacqueline Bloch

current_position.institution: Centre de Nanosciences et de Nanotechnologies (C2N), CNRS / Universite Paris-Saclay
current_position.title: Research Director (CNRS)

short_bio: Jacqueline Bloch is a French physicist known for experiments on exciton-polaritons in semiconductor microcavities and their use for quantum simulation of light.

name: Jan-Michael Rost

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems
current_position.title: Director, Finite Systems Division

short_bio: Jan-Michael Rost is a theoretical physicist and director at the MPI for the Physics of Complex Systems, working on ultracold Rydberg systems and ultrafast atomic dynamics.

name: Jay Gupta
short_bio: Jay Gupta is an experimental physicist at Ohio State using scanning tunneling microscopy to build and probe atomic-scale structures and spins.

name: Jelena Vuckovic

current_position.title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Applied Physics

short_bio: Jelena Vuckovic is an engineer-physicist at Stanford and a leader in quantum nanophotonics, photonic crystal cavities and color-center quantum devices.

name: Jelmer Renema
short_bio: Jelmer Renema is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on photonic quantum computing and the theory of boson sampling.

name: John M. Doyle

current_position.title: Henry B. Silsbee Professor of Physics

education.note: Co-advised by Thomas J. Greytak; thesis on magnetic trapping of atomic hydrogen.

short_bio: John M. Doyle is an experimental physicist at Harvard, the Henry B. Silsbee Professor of Physics and a co-director of the MIT-Harvard Center for Ultracold Atoms. He earned a BS in electrical engineering (1986) and a PhD in physics (1991) at MIT, advised by Daniel Kleppner and Thomas J. Greytak, with thesis work on the magnetic trapping of atomic hydrogen.

name: Jorg Schmiedmayer
short_bio: Jorg Schmiedmayer is an experimental physicist at TU Wien known for atom chips, matter-wave interferometry and quantum simulation of many-body dynamics with ultracold atoms.

name: Jose Ignacio Latorre

current_position.institution: University of Barcelona / Technology Innovation Institute
current_position.title: Professor of Theoretical Physics

short_bio: Jose Ignacio Latorre is a theoretical physicist working on quantum information, tensor networks and quantum machine learning, and has led quantum-technology institutes in Singapore and Abu Dhabi.

name: Josh Nunn
short_bio: Josh Nunn is a physicist at the University of Bath working on photonic quantum memories and quantum light-matter interfaces.

name: Juan Pablo Paz
short_bio: Juan Pablo Paz is a theoretical physicist at the University of Buenos Aires known for work on decoherence, quantum information and the quantum-to-classical transition.

name: K. Birgitta Whaley

current_position.title: Professor of Chemistry; Director, Berkeley Quantum Information & Computation Center

short_bio: K. Birgitta Whaley is a theoretical chemist at UC Berkeley working on quantum information, quantum control and quantum effects in biological systems.

name: Keith Burnett
short_bio: Keith Burnett is a theoretical AMO physicist known for work on ultracold atoms and Bose-Einstein condensates; he later served as a university vice-chancellor.

name: Klaus Boller
short_bio: Klaus Boller is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on laser physics, nonlinear and integrated optics.

name: Kyungwon An
short_bio: Kyungwon An is an experimental physicist at Seoul National University known for cavity quantum electrodynamics and the single-atom laser (microlaser).

name: Lu Jeu Sham
short_bio: Lu Jeu Sham is a condensed-matter theorist at UC San Diego, co-developer of the Kohn-Sham density functional theory and a contributor to semiconductor spin-coherence and spintronics.

name: Leo Kouwenhoven
short_bio: Leo Kouwenhoven is an experimental physicist at TU Delft known for semiconductor quantum dots and experiments on Majorana zero modes for topological quantum computing.

name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
short_bio: Lieven Vandersypen is an experimental physicist at TU Delft/QuTech and a leader in semiconductor spin qubits; he earlier helped demonstrate Shor's algorithm with NMR.

name: Markus Oberthaler
short_bio: Markus Oberthaler is an experimental physicist at Heidelberg working on atom interferometry, spin-squeezing and quantum simulation with Bose-Einstein condensates.

name: Martin Plenio

current_position.title: Professor of Theoretical Physics; Director, Institute of Theoretical Physics

short_bio: Martin Plenio is a theoretical physicist at Ulm known for foundational work on entanglement theory, quantum information and quantum effects in biology and NV-diamond sensing.

name: Matthias Weidemuller
short_bio: Matthias Weidemuller is an experimental physicist at Heidelberg working on ultracold atoms and molecules and Rydberg-atom quantum simulation.

name: Michael G. Raymer
short_bio: Michael Raymer is an experimental physicist at the University of Oregon known for quantum optics and a leading advocate for the U.S. National Quantum Initiative.

name: Michael S. Chapman
short_bio: Michael Chapman is an experimental physicist at Georgia Tech working on Bose-Einstein condensates, spinor gases and atom-cavity quantum optics.

name: Michel Orrit
short_bio: Michel Orrit is an experimental physicist at Leiden University and a pioneer of single-molecule optical detection and spectroscopy.

name: Mikko Mottonen
short_bio: Mikko Mottonen is an experimental physicist at Aalto University working on superconducting qubits and quantum thermodynamics, and a co-founder of IQM Quantum Computers.

name: Neil B. Manson
short_bio: Neil Manson is an experimental physicist at the ANU and a pioneer of the optical and spin physics of the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond.

name: Niek van Hulst

current_position.institution: ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences
current_position.title: ICREA Professor

short_bio: Niek van Hulst is an experimental physicist at ICFO working on nano-optics, single-molecule and single-emitter photonics and ultrafast nanoscopy.

name: Paolo Villoresi
short_bio: Paolo Villoresi is an experimental physicist at the University of Padua known for quantum communication over long distances and satellite quantum key distribution.

name: Paul L. McEuen

current_position.title: John A. Newman Professor of Physical Science

short_bio: Paul McEuen is an experimental physicist at Cornell known for nanoscience, carbon-nanotube and graphene devices, and atomic-scale machines.

name: Paul Vitanyi
short_bio: Paul Vitanyi is a theoretical computer scientist at CWI known for Kolmogorov complexity and contributions to the theory of quantum computation.

name: Pepijn Pinkse
short_bio: Pepijn Pinkse is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on quantum optics, complex photonic media and physical-layer security.

name: Peter Lambropoulos
short_bio: Peter Lambropoulos is a theoretical AMO physicist known for multiphoton and strong-field atomic processes and quantum optics.

name: Peter Leek
short_bio: Peter Leek is an experimental physicist at Oxford developing superconducting qubits and the coaxial-circuit (3D-integrated) approach to scalable processors.

name: Peter Mosley
short_bio: Peter Mosley is an experimental physicist at the University of Bath working on fibre-based single-photon sources and integrated quantum photonics.

name: Peter Schmelcher
short_bio: Peter Schmelcher is a theoretical physicist at the University of Hamburg working on quantum dynamics of complex atomic and molecular systems and ultracold few-body physics.

name: Pierre Rouchon
short_bio: Pierre Rouchon is a control theorist at Mines Paris known for quantum control and feedback stabilization, including work underpinning cavity-QED and cat-qubit experiments.

name: Randy Hulet

current_position.title: Fayez Sarofim Professor of Physics & Astronomy

short_bio: Randy Hulet is an experimental physicist at Rice University known for early Bose-Einstein condensation with attractive interactions and ultracold-atom quantum simulation.

name: Richard N. Zare

current_position.title: Marguerite Blake Wilbur Professor in Natural Science

short_bio: Richard Zare is a chemist at Stanford renowned for laser studies of chemical reactions and the development of laser-induced fluorescence.

name: Robert A. Buhrman

current_position.title: J. E. Sweet Professor of Engineering, Emeritus

short_bio: Robert Buhrman is an applied physicist at Cornell known for nanoscale magnetism and spintronics, including spin-torque devices for memory.

name: Robert M. Westervelt

current_position.title: Mallinckrodt Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

short_bio: Robert Westervelt is an experimental physicist at Harvard working on nanoscale and mesoscopic electronic systems and scanned-probe imaging.

name: Roberta Ramponi
short_bio: Roberta Ramponi is an experimental physicist at Politecnico di Milano known for integrated and laser-written photonics for quantum applications.

name: Rodolfo Miranda

current_position.institution: Autonomous University of Madrid / IMDEA Nanoscience
current_position.title: Professor of Physics

short_bio: Rodolfo Miranda is an experimental physicist in Madrid known for surface science, nanomagnetism and scanning-probe studies of low-dimensional materials.

name: Ronald L. Walsworth
short_bio: Ronald Walsworth is an experimental physicist at the University of Maryland and a leader in NV-diamond quantum sensing and precision measurement.

name: Shinji Urabe
short_bio: Shinji Urabe is an experimental physicist at Osaka University known for trapped-ion quantum information and laser cooling of calcium ions.

name: Stephan Reitzenstein
short_bio: Stephan Reitzenstein is an experimental physicist at TU Berlin working on semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and nanophotonic devices.

name: Steven Prawer
short_bio: Steven Prawer is an experimental physicist at the University of Melbourne known for diamond-based quantum technologies and color-center engineering.

name: Charles Stuart Adams
short_bio: Stuart Adams is an experimental physicist at Durham University known for Rydberg-atom quantum optics, Rydberg electrometry and nonlinear optics with cold atoms.

name: Thomas F. Gallagher

current_position.title: Jesse W. Beams Professor of Physics

short_bio: Thomas Gallagher is an experimental physicist at the University of Virginia and a leading authority on Rydberg atoms, author of the standard monograph Rydberg Atoms.

name: Tilman Pfau
short_bio: Tilman Pfau is an experimental physicist at the University of Stuttgart known for dipolar quantum gases, quantum droplets and Rydberg-atom physics.

name: Timothy P. Softley
short_bio: Timothy Softley is a physical chemist and Professor of Chemistry at the University of Birmingham, known for cold-molecule and ion-molecule reaction dynamics. His group pioneered the study of low-temperature reactions between laser-cooled calcium-ion (Ca⁺) Coulomb crystals and velocity-selected cold polar molecules such as methyl fluoride (CH₃F) and 1,2-dichloroethene, monitoring state- and isomer-selective reaction rates by imaging the ion fluorescence and forming sympathetically cooled molecular ions including CaF⁺.

name: Tord Claeson
short_bio: Tord Claeson is an experimental physicist at Chalmers known for superconductivity, Josephson junctions and superconducting quantum devices.

name: Wonho Jhe
short_bio: Wonho Jhe is an experimental physicist at Seoul National University working on atom optics, near-field optics and high-sensitivity nanomechanical sensing.

name: Yoshihisa Yamamoto
short_bio: Yoshihisa Yamamoto is a physicist at Stanford and NTT known for quantum optics, single-photon sources and the coherent Ising machine approach to optical computing.

name: Mark Thompson
short_bio: Mark Thompson is an experimental physicist at the University of Bristol and a pioneer of silicon integrated quantum photonics; he co-founded PsiQuantum.

name: Ran Finkelstein

current_position.title: Senior Lecturer, School of Physics and Astronomy

postdocs.note: Troesh Postdoctoral Prize Fellowship (2021–2024); work on alkaline-earth neutral-atom arrays and high-fidelity Rydberg control.

short_bio: Dr. Ran Finkelstein is an experimental physicist and Senior Lecturer in the School of Physics and Astronomy at Tel Aviv University, where he leads a laboratory on quantum information with atoms and photons. His research spans quantum computation, quantum metrology, and quantum simulation with arrays of ultracold neutral atoms held in optical tweezers, as well as quantum optics — the generation, storage, and interaction of single photons with atomic ensembles.

name: Ksenia Khabarova
short_bio: Ksenia Khabarova is an experimental physicist at the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) and the Russian Quantum Center in Moscow, working on trapped-ion quantum computing with ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) ions and on optical atomic clocks and precision frequency metrology. She is part of the joint FIAN–RQC group that built Russia's ion-based quantum computer using qudit (ququart) encoding.

name: Nikolai Kolachevsky
short_bio: Nikolai Kolachevsky is an experimental physicist and Director of the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow. He co-leads the joint FIAN–Russian Quantum Center trapped-ion programme that built Russia's ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) qudit-based quantum computer, and has a long record in optical atomic clocks and precision spectroscopy.

name: Ilya Semerikov
short_bio: Ilya Semerikov is an experimental physicist at the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) and the Russian Quantum Center in Moscow, and a laureate of the VYZOV national prize. He led the development of Russia's ion-based quantum computer, which uses ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) ions in a linear trap with qudit (ququart) encoding and was reported at the 50-qubit scale in 2024.

name: Tanya Zelevinsky
short_bio: Tanya Zelevinsky is a Professor of Physics at Columbia University, where her ZLab uses high-precision spectroscopy of ultracold molecules to test fundamental physics. She built a molecular lattice clock based on quantized vibrations of ultracold strontium dimers (Sr2) and studies ultracold molecular photodissociation and quantum-state control of diatomic molecules.

name: Sebastian Will
short_bio: Sebastian Will is an Associate Professor of Physics at Columbia University, where his group creates dipolar quantum matter from ultracold polar molecules. The Will Lab assembles ground-state sodium-cesium (NaCs) molecules, including in optical tweezer arrays, to explore dipolar many-body physics, ultracold chemistry and molecular qubits.

name: Michael Tarbutt
short_bio: Michael Tarbutt is a Professor of Physics at Imperial College London and a leader of the Centre for Cold Matter. His group laser-cools, slows and magneto-optically traps calcium monofluoride (CaF) molecules, develops molecules as a platform for quantum computation and simulation, and uses laser-cooled ytterbium monofluoride (YbF) to measure the electron's electric dipole moment.

name: Nicholas Hutzler
short_bio: Nicholas Hutzler leads a group at the California Institute of Technology that develops cold and ultracold polyatomic molecules — such as calcium monohydroxide (CaOH) and ytterbium monohydroxide (YbOH) — as quantum sensors for precision searches of physics beyond the Standard Model, including the electron's electric dipole moment.

name: Lawrence Cheuk
short_bio: Lawrence Cheuk is an Assistant Professor of Physics at Princeton University, where his group builds optical-tweezer arrays of ultracold molecules — including calcium monofluoride (CaF) and sodium-cesium (NaCs) — for quantum simulation, quantum information and precision measurement.

name: Silke Ospelkaus
short_bio: Silke Ospelkaus is a Professor of Physics at Leibniz University Hannover, where her group produces ultracold ground-state polar molecules — sodium-potassium (NaK) and potassium-rubidium (KRb) — to study ultracold chemistry, dipolar collisions and quantum-controlled reactions.

name: Martin Zwierlein
short_bio: Martin Zwierlein is a Professor of Physics at MIT and a member of the MIT-Harvard Center for Ultracold Atoms, where his group studies strongly interacting ultracold Fermi gases and ultracold dipolar molecules. His laboratory created ultracold gases of fermionic sodium-potassium (NaK) molecules in their absolute ground state.

name: Loïc Anderegg
short_bio: Loïc Anderegg is an Assistant Professor of Physics at the University of Southern California, where his group develops optical-tweezer arrays of laser-cooled diatomic and polyatomic molecules for quantum science, including calcium monofluoride (CaF) and calcium monohydroxide (CaOH).

name: Stefan Truppe

current_position.institution: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
current_position.title: Research Group Leader

postdocs.institution: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society

short_bio: Stefan Truppe leads a research group at the Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society in Berlin, where he develops laser cooling and trapping of molecules — notably aluminium monofluoride (AlF), a promising candidate for deep laser cooling — and high-resolution molecular spectroscopy.

name: Gerard Meijer

current_position.institution: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
current_position.title: Director, Molecular Physics

short_bio: Gerard Meijer is a Director at the Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society and a pioneer of the manipulation of cold molecules. With Hendrick Bethlem he invented the Stark decelerator, using time-varying electric fields to slow and trap polar molecular beams, opening the field of controlled cold-molecule physics and chemistry.

name: Bas van de Meerakker
short_bio: Bas (Sebastiaan) van de Meerakker is a Professor of Physics at Radboud University Nijmegen, where his group uses Stark-decelerated molecular beams to study cold molecular collisions with full quantum-state resolution, revealing scattering resonances in benchmark systems such as OH, NO and NH3.

name: Hendrick Bethlem
short_bio: Hendrick Bethlem is an Associate Professor of Physics at VU Amsterdam, where his group develops decelerated and trapped cold-molecule beams for precision tests of fundamental physics, including searches for a possible variation of the proton-to-electron mass ratio using methanol spectroscopy and a molecular fountain.

name: Steven Hoekstra
short_bio: Steven Hoekstra is a Professor of Physics at the University of Groningen, where he develops decelerated and slow beams of heavy polar molecules — strontium monofluoride (SrF) and barium monofluoride (BaF) — for precision tests of fundamental symmetries.

name: Tim Langen
short_bio: Tim Langen is a Professor of Physics at TU Wien, where he leads the Cold Molecules and Quantum Technologies division at the Atominstitut. His group develops laser cooling of aluminium monofluoride (AlF) molecules, a candidate for producing dense samples of ultracold molecules for quantum technology.

name: Amar Vutha
short_bio: Amar Vutha is an Associate Professor of Physics at the University of Toronto, where his group pursues precision measurements with molecules to search for physics beyond the Standard Model, including a novel approach to the electron's electric dipole moment using polar molecules frozen into a solid inert-gas (neon) matrix.

name: Chin-Wen Chou
short_bio: Chin-Wen (James) Chou is a staff scientist in the Ion Storage Group at NIST Boulder, where he applies quantum-logic techniques developed for trapped-ion clocks to control single molecular ions. His group prepared and coherently manipulated pure quantum states of a single calcium hydride ion (CaH+), enabling quantum-logic spectroscopy of molecular ions.

name: David Leibrandt
short_bio: David Leibrandt is a Professor of Physics at UCLA, where his group develops next-generation optical atomic clocks and precision measurements, including aluminium-ion (Al+) quantum-logic clocks, quantum-logic spectroscopy of molecular ions, and proposals for many-ion Coulomb-crystal clocks.

name: Stephan Schiller
short_bio: Stephan Schiller is a Professor of Physics at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, where his group performs ultra-high-precision spectroscopy of trapped molecular hydrogen ions — HD+ and H2+ — to test quantum electrodynamics, determine fundamental constants such as the proton-to-electron mass ratio, and search for new physics.

name: Roland Wester
short_bio: Roland Wester is a Professor of Physics at the University of Innsbruck, where his group studies the dynamics of cold molecular ions and anions in radiofrequency multipole ion traps, using velocity-map imaging to reveal the mechanisms of fundamental ion-molecule reactions such as nucleophilic substitution (SN2).

name: Brianna Heazlewood
short_bio: Brianna Heazlewood is a Professor of Physical Chemistry at the University of Liverpool, where her group studies cold, controlled chemical reactions between trapped molecular ions held in Coulomb crystals and velocity-selected beams of neutral radicals produced by a Zeeman decelerator, probing reaction dynamics at low temperatures with full control over the reactants.

name: Jeremy Hutson
short_bio: Jeremy Hutson is a Professor of Chemistry at Durham University and a leading theorist of ultracold molecules and molecular collisions. His work underpins the formation of ultracold molecules by magnetoassociation and STIRAP, the theory of Feshbach resonances, and the understanding of collisions and intermolecular forces in cold molecular gases such as RbCs.

name: John Bohn

current_position.title: Fellow of JILA and Professor Adjoint

short_bio: John Bohn is a Fellow of JILA and Professor Adjoint at the University of Colorado Boulder, working on the theory of ultracold molecules, dipolar collisions and cold controlled chemistry. His theoretical work has guided landmark experiments on quantum-state-controlled reactions and dipolar collisions of ultracold KRb molecules.

name: Svetlana Kotochigova
short_bio: Svetlana Kotochigova is a Professor of Physics at Temple University and a theorist of the electronic structure, interactions and collisions of ultracold atoms and molecules. Her calculations of molecular potentials, transition dipole moments and Feshbach resonances guide experiments that create and control ultracold polar molecules such as KRb and RbCs.

name: Olivier Dulieu

current_position.institution: French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS)
current_position.title: Senior Researcher (Directeur de Recherche)

short_bio: Olivier Dulieu is a CNRS Senior Researcher at the Laboratoire Aimé Cotton (Université Paris-Saclay) and a theorist of cold and ultracold molecules. His work established the theoretical foundations for forming cold molecules by photoassociation and for transferring them to their absolute ground state, and provides the molecular structure and interaction data underpinning ultracold-molecule experiments worldwide.

name: Tijs Karman
short_bio: Tijs Karman is an Associate Professor of Physics at Radboud University Nijmegen and a theorist of ultracold molecular collisions. He developed the theory of microwave shielding of ultracold polar molecules — engineering repulsive shields with microwave fields to suppress lossy collisions — which enabled experiments to evaporatively cool dipolar molecules to quantum degeneracy and to a dipolar molecular Bose-Einstein condensate.

name: Christiane Koch
short_bio: Christiane Koch is a Professor of Physics at Freie Universität Berlin and a leading theorist of quantum control. Her work develops optimal-control methods for steering molecular dynamics — including the control of molecular rotation, the formation and stabilization of ultracold molecules, and control of open quantum systems — with broad applications across quantum technologies.

name: Cheng Chin
short_bio: Cheng Chin is a Professor of Physics at the University of Chicago, where his group studies ultracold cesium (Cs) gases as a tunable platform for quantum many-body physics, using Feshbach resonances to control interactions. His lab has explored Efimov few-body physics, quantum simulation of phase transitions, and analogues of cosmological and condensed-matter phenomena in cold atoms.

name: Waseem Bakr
short_bio: Waseem Bakr is a Professor of Physics at Princeton University, where his group uses quantum-gas microscopy to image and manipulate ultracold fermionic lithium (Li) and potassium (K) — and dipolar erbium (Er) — atom by atom in optical lattices and tweezers, probing the Fermi-Hubbard model and strongly correlated quantum matter.

name: Monika Schleier-Smith
short_bio: Monika Schleier-Smith is an Associate Professor of Physics at Stanford University, where her group engineers programmable interactions among rubidium (Rb) atoms coupled to optical cavities, using cavity quantum electrodynamics to generate spin-squeezed and entangled states for quantum metrology and to build tunable-range quantum simulators.

name: Mark Kasevich
short_bio: Mark Kasevich is a Professor of Physics at Stanford University and a pioneer of light-pulse atom interferometry, using freely falling cesium (Cs) and rubidium (Rb) atoms as ultra-precise inertial and gravitational sensors. His group develops atomic gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers, very-long-baseline atom interferometers for tests of gravity and searches for dark matter and gravitational waves, and spin-squeezing for quantum-enhanced sensing.

name: Holger Müller
short_bio: Holger Müller is a Professor of Physics at the University of California, Berkeley, where his group builds precision atom interferometers with cesium (Cs) atoms to test fundamental physics. His measurement of the fine-structure constant via the recoil of cesium atoms is among the most precise tests of the Standard Model and of quantum electrodynamics.

name: Selim Jochim
short_bio: Selim Jochim is a Professor of Physics at Heidelberg University, where his group builds strongly interacting Fermi gases of lithium (Li) atom by atom, deterministically preparing few-fermion systems to study how many-body behaviour emerges from individual particles.

name: Giacomo Roati
short_bio: Giacomo Roati is a CNR-INO senior researcher at the LENS laboratory of the University of Florence, where his group studies ultracold fermionic lithium (Li) and potassium (K) gases as quantum simulators of superfluidity, transport and disorder. His lab has observed Josephson dynamics and superfluidity in strongly interacting Fermi gases and Anderson localization of matter waves.

name: Rudolf Grimm
short_bio: Rudolf Grimm is a Professor of Physics at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI), where his groups study strongly interacting ultracold gases of lithium (Li), cesium (Cs) and erbium (Er). His work produced the first molecular Bose-Einstein condensate, fermionic superfluidity in the BEC-BCS crossover, the first observation of Efimov states, and dipolar quantum gases of erbium.

name: Francesca Ferlaino
short_bio: Francesca Ferlaino is a Professor of Physics at the University of Innsbruck and a director at the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI), where her group creates strongly dipolar quantum gases of the magnetic lanthanides erbium (Er) and dysprosium (Dy). Her lab achieved Bose-Einstein condensation of erbium and observed dipolar quantum droplets and supersolid states of matter.

name: Monika Aidelsburger
short_bio: Monika Aidelsburger is a Professor of Physics at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, where her group engineers artificial gauge fields and topological band structures for ultracold rubidium (Rb) and potassium (K) atoms in optical lattices using Floquet (periodic-driving) techniques, realizing the Hofstadter model and measuring topological invariants.

name: Hans-Christoph Nägerl
short_bio: Hans-Christoph Nägerl is a Professor of Physics at the University of Innsbruck, where his group studies ultracold cesium (Cs) gases and Feshbach molecules, including one-dimensional quantum gases (Tonks-Girardeau and sine-Gordon physics) and the creation of ultracold ground-state Cs2 and RbCs molecules.

name: David Allcock

postdocs.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder

short_bio: David Allcock is an Assistant Professor of Physics at the University of Oregon, where his group develops trapped-ion quantum computing with calcium ions (40Ca+), focusing on microfabricated surface-electrode ion traps, laser-free microwave control of qubits, and integrated photonics and electronics for scalable processors.

name: Vladimir Manucharyan

current_position.institution: EPFL – Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne
current_position.title: Professor of Physics

short_bio: Vladimir Manucharyan is a Professor of Physics at EPFL (and formerly the University of Maryland), where his group develops protected superconducting qubits. He invented the fluxonium qubit — a superconducting circuit built from a Josephson junction shunted by a large 'superinductance' that is insensitive to charge noise — and pursues high-coherence, intrinsically protected qubit designs using high-kinetic-inductance superinductors.

name: Chen Wang
short_bio: Chen Wang is an Associate Professor of Physics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where his group develops bosonic superconducting qubits — encoding error-correctable logical qubits in the states of high-quality three-dimensional microwave cavities controlled by transmon ancillas.

name: Britton Plourde
short_bio: Britton Plourde is a Professor of Physics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (previously at Syracuse University, 2005-2024), working on superconducting qubits and microwave circuits. His group studies coherence-limiting materials defects, quasiparticles and superconducting vortices, develops transmon and flux qubits and resonators, and pursues single-flux-quantum (SFQ) digital control for scalable superconducting processors.

name: Kater Murch
short_bio: Kater Murch is a Professor of Physics at Washington University in St. Louis, where his group studies the quantum measurement and control of superconducting qubits. His experiments tracked the individual quantum trajectories of a continuously monitored transmon and stabilized its dynamics with real-time feedback, and his group explores non-Hermitian physics and exceptional points in driven dissipative quantum circuits.

name: Daniel Esteve

current_position.institution: French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA)
current_position.title: Emeritus Director of Research (CEA)

short_bio: Daniel Esteve is a senior physicist who led the Quantronics group at CEA Saclay, a pioneering laboratory of superconducting quantum circuits. With Denis Vion and Michel Devoret, his group built the 'quantronium' — an early superconducting qubit operated at a noise-insensitive 'sweet spot' that achieved long coherence — and made foundational studies of single-Cooper-pair and single-electron devices and of decoherence in Josephson-junction qubits.

name: Andrea Morello
short_bio: Andrea Morello is a Professor of Physics at UNSW Sydney who builds spin qubits from single phosphorus donor atoms implanted in silicon. His group demonstrated single-atom electron- and nuclear-spin qubits with high-fidelity readout and control, record coherence times, and small nuclear-spin quantum processors — a route to silicon-based quantum computing compatible with existing microelectronics.

name: Andrew Dzurak
short_bio: Andrew Dzurak is a Professor of Physics at UNSW Sydney who develops silicon spin qubits in metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) quantum dots, fabricated with CMOS-compatible processes for scalability. His group demonstrated the first two-qubit logic gate in silicon and high-fidelity addressable spin qubits.

name: Menno Veldhorst
short_bio: Menno Veldhorst is an Associate Professor at Delft University of Technology (QuTech) who develops semiconductor spin qubits in silicon and germanium quantum dots. He was first author on the first two-qubit logic gate in silicon and built a four-qubit germanium quantum processor based on hole spins, pursuing dense, scalable quantum-dot arrays.

name: Jason Petta
short_bio: Jason Petta is a Professor of Physics at UCLA (previously Princeton) who develops semiconductor quantum-dot spin qubits in GaAs and silicon. His work established coherent control of singlet-triplet spin qubits, demonstrated a coherent spin-photon interface coupling a single spin to a microwave photon, and realized two-qubit gates in silicon.

name: Seigo Tarucha
short_bio: Seigo Tarucha is a team leader at the RIKEN Center for Quantum Computing and Professor Emeritus at the University of Tokyo who pioneered the physics of few-electron semiconductor quantum dots (revealing atom-like shell structure) and now develops high-fidelity spin qubits in gallium-arsenide and silicon quantum dots, reaching gate fidelities above the fault-tolerance threshold.

name: Ferdinand Kuemmeth
short_bio: Ferdinand Kuemmeth is a Professor of Physics at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen who develops semiconductor spin qubits in gallium-arsenide and germanium quantum-dot arrays, with a focus on scalable control and readout of multi-qubit registers.
